newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain summons Portuguese envoy over ETA case.
newsitem.headline: Spain summons Portuguese envoy over ETA case.

text.p: Spain summoned Portugal's ambassador on Monday to convey its anger at the refusal of a Portuguese court to hand over a suspected ETA rebel.
The Portuguese embassy confirmed ambassador Leonardo Matheas had been called in by the Foreign Ministry to discuss the court decision but would not provide details of the meeting.
"The ambassador was called in to the ministry and met with Deputy Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs Jose Carvajal," an embassy spokesman told Reuters.

Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes threatened on Friday to summon the ambassador after the Portuguese court freed Jose Luis Telletxea, wanted in Spain for smuggling ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) rebels and weapons across the northern border with France.
The minister said the Portuguese courts should have respected the opinion of Spanish courts which characterised Telletxea's actions as a crime in Spain.

Matutes said Spain was considering reestablishing border checkpoints now that Telletxea was free to prevent him crossing back into Spain with impunity and committing other crimes. About 800 people have been killed in ETA's 29-year campaign for independence from Spain.
